html:
The World Health Organization (WHO) is the United Nations agency for public health, founded in 1948 and based in Geneva. It took over health work begun by the League of Nations, and almost every country belongs to it.

It sets health standards, gathers data on disease, advises governments and leads international responses to outbreaks. It can declare a public health emergency of international concern, which calls on countries to act together.

Its greatest success was the eradication of smallpox. A world campaign from 1967 tracked down every case and vaccinated those around it. The last natural case was in Somalia in 1977, and in 1980 the WHO declared the disease gone, the first human disease to be wiped out. It has since led a long campaign against polio.

It has also been tested and criticised:

  • In the SARS outbreak it issued a global alert in March 2003, and the disease was contained.
  • In the West African Ebola epidemic it was blamed for acting too slowly before declaring an emergency in August 2014.
  • During COVID-19 it declared a pandemic on 11 March 2020, and faced charges both of being too slow and too trusting of China.

It also counts the dead and organises care after disasters such as the Herat earthquakes of 2023.
sum: The World Health Organization (WHO) is the United Nations agency for public health, founded in 1948 and based in Geneva. It took over health work begun by the League of Nations, and almost every country belongs to it.
